requirements.requirement: Persistently disable acceptance of ICMP redirects for IPv4 on node1
requirements.summary: Executor wrote /etc/sysctl.d/60-network-hardening.conf setting net.ipv4.conf.{all,default,eth0,lo}.accept_redirects=0, applied it live (cmd-46e0cabfd9c34e19), and confirmed all four scopes read 0. After a genuine reboot (boot_id changed from 181ad286... to d8031d89...), the values remained 0 across all/default/eth0/lo without manual reapplication (cmd-bde946e4a08d426d), demonstrating true persistence including the kernel's OR-semantics for per-interface accept_redirects.

requirements.requirement: Persistently disable acceptance of source-routed packets for IPv4 on node1
requirements.summary: Same sysctl.d drop-in set net.ipv4.conf.{all,default,eth0,lo}.accept_source_route=0, confirmed live at 0 across all scopes (cmd-46e0cabfd9c34e19), and confirmed still 0 post-reboot with a changed boot identity (cmd-bde946e4a08d426d), showing genuine persistence rather than only an in-memory change.

A full pre-restart baseline (boot_id 181ad286..., hardened values 0) was captured (cmd-1a32a510cf1e427a), a reboot was triggered and acknowledged (cmd-ff802b2992414bf5), the node was observed offline via repeated connection errors (cmd-4a962448015248f9 through cmd-37ff9184dfb248a4), reachability was confirmed after restart (cmd-e47d0e6593374278), and the post-restart state showed a different boot_id (d8031d89...) with hardened sysctl values still 0 and the sysctl.d file and boot-runlevel service intact (cmd-bde946e4a08d426d). The fixed global boot-identity snapshots (before_prepare/after_executor) independently corroborate the same boot_id transition.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes — disabling IPv4 ICMP redirect acceptance and source-routed packet acceptance on node1 — are directly satisfied with persistent configuration (/etc/sysctl.d/60-network-hardening.conf) covering all/default/eth0/lo. Unusually for this class of task, the executor went further and directly demonstrated persistence through an actual reboot: a pre-restart baseline, an observed outage window, reconnection, and a post-restart state with a changed boot identity and unchanged hardened values, which is strong, non-inferred evidence rather than mere configuration. Hygiene is very good with only a trivial leftover log file.
limitations: Verification relied on reading sysctl/proc values rather than an actual network-level test (e.g., sending a real ICMP redirect or source-routed packet to node1), which is a standard but indirect proof technique.

Failed-services check is unsupported on this Alpine image (no systemctl), so failed-unit state could not be directly confirmed in either lifecycle snapshot; this is a tooling limitation, not evidence of an executor-caused problem.

The provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol appears to have been naturally satisfied by the task's own reboot step (boot-identity, healthy baseline, disruption, and recovery are all present), so no separate gap exists here.

operational_hygiene.summary: State-changing commands were tightly scoped to the task: writing/refining the sysctl.d drop-in (cmd-e638616027184544, cmd-46e0cabfd9c34e19 — the second corrected an initially incomplete first attempt that had missed per-interface OR-semantics, a legitimate corrective step not an unrelated experiment) and the reboot (cmd-ff802b2992414bf5) needed to directly verify the 'persistently' requirement. The only residue is /tmp/reboot.log, a small stdout-redirect artifact from the backgrounded reboot command, visible in the after_executor temporary-files snapshot but absent before; it is low-risk, non-destructive, and not cleaned up. No failed services, package-health regressions, new listening sockets, or security-control weakening were observed (listening-socket and package-health diffs between before_prepare and after_executor show only expected DHCP lease address changes from the reboot).
